question: Should the core package updater officially preserve local packaged `dist` mutations and offer opt-in replay after update?
rationale: The implementation is technically hardened, but it creates a durable public update contract and ongoing filesystem-security and release-compatibility ownership that automated tests cannot authorize.

options.title: Support preservation and replay
options.body: Approve default recovery-bundle preservation plus the explicit replay flag and exact legacy-package policy.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep detection, recovery capture, and reporting but remove automatic replay and its public CLI flag.

options.title: Decline packaged mutations
options.body: Keep packaged installations immutable and direct customization to source installs or supported plugin surfaces.

recommendation.title: Support preservation and replay
recommendation.body: Approve default recovery-bundle preservation plus the explicit replay flag and exact legacy-package policy.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the live assignee and strongest available current-history owner across the affected update and package-integrity paths.
